newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan and Israel to set up Aqaba-Eilat consulates.
newsitem.headline: Jordan and Israel to set up Aqaba-Eilat consulates.

text.p: Jordan and Israel have agreed to set up consular services in two southern Red Sea resort towns to ease the flow of tourists between them, officials said on Thursday.
"We agreed to consular services in Aqaba and Eilat with a non-resident consul for the two countries," Fayez al-Khasawneh, head of Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba Regional Authority, told Reuters.
Khasawneh said the Aqaba-Eilat joint committee approved the proposal during a regular meeting on Wednesday, as part of moves to help tourists cross the border between the two neighbouring resorts.
Tourists and travellers landing in Jordan or Israel now need to go through embassies in Amman and Tel Aviv for visas to travel to the other side.
The southern part of Jordan is a tourist magnet, with the Nabatean rose-red carved stone city of Petra close to Aqaba. Eilat's coral beaches are also popular with tourists and scuba divers.
Khasawneh said he expected the non-resident consular services to open at the start of next year.
Jordan and Israel signed a peace treaty in October 1994, ending a 46-year-state of war between the neighbours.

Peace boosted tourism but the number of foreign visitors has slumped due to doubts about Middle East peace after the election of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in May and U.S. air strikes against Iraq in September.
